sections.skill: Compare free, subscription and pay-per-use pricing for a pattern of use

questions.prompt: What does a subscription charge?

choices.text: Only for what you actually use each month, so that light users always pay less

questions.intro: AI tools are priced in three common ways. A FREE PLAN costs nothing but usually has limits: fewer messages, slower or smaller models, or fewer features. A SUBSCRIPTION charges a fixed amount each month for a set of features, whether you use it a lot or a little. PAY-PER-USE (metered) pricing charges for what you actually use, often per amount of text processed. To compare, estimate YOUR pattern of use. Light, occasional use often fits a free plan or pay-per-use; heavy, steady use may make a subscription cheaper per task.

sections.skill: Compare AI plans with ways to pay for a gym or a bus

questions.prompt: Paying per bus ride is like which plan?
questions.intro: Paying for the BUS per ride is like pay-per-use: you pay each time. A monthly BUS PASS is like a subscription: one price, ride as much as you like. A free community walking trail is like a free plan: no cost, but limited (no rain cover, fixed hours). If you ride the bus twice a month, pay per ride. If you ride twice a day, the pass is cheaper. The right choice depends on how often you go.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.prompt: Hypothetical: an annual plan costs 120 dollars; monthly costs 15 dollars. You will only use it for 2 months. Which is cheaper?

choices.text: Annual, since annual plans are always the cheaper option no matter how long you use the tool

questions.intro: Comparisons hide details. A subscription may include features you will never use, and an annual plan may be cheaper per month but cost more if you stop after two months. Pay-per-use can surprise you if usage spikes, so set spending limits where available. Free plans may have different privacy terms from paid plans. Check whether the price includes tax, how renewal works, and how to cancel before you sign up.

questions.prompt: Why set a spending limit on pay-per-use?

Because pay-per-use plans always charge the same amount every month no matter what
Usage can spike and surprise you
